title: Transformers can now run llama.cpp-style GGUF models directly
friendlyTitle: Hugging Face makes small local AI models easier to run
summary: Hugging Face is adding direct GGUF support to Transformers, initially optimised for Qwen3.5 on Apple Silicon using llama.cpp’s underlying ggml kernels. Developers can load a quantised Hub checkpoint through the familiar Transformers API or serve it behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
friendlySummary: Transformers can now load GGUF model files, which are designed to fit large models into less memory. The first fast path focuses on Apple Silicon Macs and Qwen3.5 models.
whyItMatters: This reduces the gap between the large GGUF ecosystem used for local AI and the Python tools many developers already know. The first release has a narrow hardware and architecture focus, so users should verify memory use, speed and output quality on the exact model and machine they intend to run.
friendlyWhyItMatters: People can use familiar Python tools to run more AI work on their own computer. Check that your model and hardware are supported before expecting the fastest results.
